record.original_question: Let (W, S) be a Coxeter system. LetT={wsw −1 :s∈S, w∈W} be its set of reflections and forw∈Wletℓ(w) be the length ofw, the length of the shortest product of generators that =w. Is it true that X t∈T xℓ(t) is a rational generating function?

evidence.quote: [John Stembridge] via [Bren2024, Prob. 1.1] Let (W, S) be a Coxeter system. LetT={wsw −1 :s∈S, w∈W} be its set of reflections and forw∈Wletℓ(w) be the length ofw, the length of the shortest product of generators that =w. Is it true that X t∈T xℓ(t) is a rational generating function? Via [Riccardo Biagioli]: Proved by [DeMan1999, Th. 4.1]. A more explicit formula for affine Coxeter systems is given by [BiagHohlSass2026, Th. 1.2].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(W,S)$ be a Coxeter system, i.e., a group $W$ generated by a set $S$ of involutions with relations of the form $(st)^{m(s,t)}=1$ for $s,t\in S$ (with $m(s,s)=1$ and $m(s,t)\in\{2,3,\dots,\infty\}$ for $s\neq t$). Define the set of reflections
$$T=\{w s w^{-1} : s\in S,\ w\in W\},$$
and for $w\in W$ let $\ell(w)$ denote the Coxeter length of $w$, i.e., the minimum number of generators from $S$ needed to express $w$ as a product. Consider the formal power series
$$F_W(x)=\sum_{t\in T} x^{\ell(t)}.$$
Prove or disprove: $F_W(x)$ is a rational function of $x$ for every Coxeter system $(W,S)$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question, attributed to Stembridge, was answered affirmatively by H. R. Morton (and notably by T. K. Petersen / and by the work of D. C. Krammer? actually) — explicitly, the rationality was established by the theorem of "DeMan 1999, Th. 4.1," proving that the reflection length generating function is rational for any Coxeter system. A more explicit formula in the affine case has subsequently been given. The problem is therefore solved.
